macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S.-Iran tensions drove a fresh oil spike and market volatility
items.summary: Reuters reported that renewed U.S. strikes on Iran lifted oil prices and kept investors focused on inflation risks, while Wall Street futures and European shares traded cautiously in choppy conditions. Asian markets also advanced, but gains were capped by the jump in crude and bond-market pressure.

items.title: Oil surged as fears of Strait of Hormuz disruptions returned
items.summary: Yahoo Finance and Al Jazeera both reported that crude rose sharply after the fragile U.S.-Iran ceasefire broke down, with Brent moving above $76 a barrel and WTI closing at a two-week high. Travel stocks weakened while energy shares benefited from the move.

items.title: Central banks remained in focus as inflation worries resurfaced
items.summary: Reuters highlighted that rising oil prices revived rate-hike bets and kept the U.S. dollar firm, while the 10-year Japanese government bond yield hit a 30-year high on renewed inflation concerns. Financial Times coverage also noted that some Federal Reserve officials still saw a need for future rate increases to contain inflation.

items.title: U.S. stock futures and global equities steadied after the latest geopolitical shock
items.summary: Reuters said U.S. stock index futures edged higher as markets digested the Iran-related flare-up, while European shares recovered in uneven trading and Asian stocks climbed as semiconductors bounced. The broader tone remained fragile because higher oil prices threatened to delay any easing in inflation.

items.title: PepsiCo posted stronger revenue but warned about weaker North American demand
items.summary: Yahoo Finance reported that PepsiCo's second-quarter net revenue rose 6.4% to $24.2 billion, beating expectations even as the company said North American consumers were tightening their budgets. CNBC also flagged PepsiCo as one of the biggest premarket movers after a mixed earnings reaction.

items.title: Chip stocks rallied while Treasury yields steadied
items.summary: CNBC reported that semiconductor shares were jumping again in premarket trading, helping stabilize risk sentiment after the earlier oil-driven selloff. U.S. Treasury yields were little changed after the prior session's spike.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent inside its chatbot designed to execute tasks across applications and files, intensifying competition in professional AI tools. The move reflects a broader push toward agentic systems that can perform multi-step office workflows.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-Live voice models for real-time conversation
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The release highlights continued rapid progress in low-latency multimodal AI.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to its Muse Spark AI model and an upgraded version, positioning it directly against paid AI offerings from Anthropic and OpenAI. The announcement signals Meta's push to monetize and expand its model ecosystem.

items.title: SpaceXAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: SpaceXAI announced Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model yet and optimized for coding and agentic workflows. The launch adds to the recent wave of frontier-model releases focused on task execution rather than chat alone.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body meant to keep the company aligned with its public mission. The move underscores growing governance and safety oversight in advanced AI companies.

items.title: Trump administration lifts restrictions on Anthropic Claude models
items.summary: The Trump administration lifted restrictions on Anthropic's latest Claude chatbot versions after a weekslong ban tied to cybersecurity concerns. The decision suggests U.S. regulators are still actively shaping which frontier models can be deployed more broadly.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly faces government-requested limits on GPT-5.6 Sol
items.summary: AP reported that OpenAI is restricting release of its new GPT-5.6 Sol model at the request of the Trump administration. The report points to continued government involvement in the rollout of advanced AI systems.

items.title: Meta plans to begin manufacturing an AI chip in September
items.summary: Reuters reported that Meta plans to start manufacturing an artificial intelligence chip from September as it expands computing capacity for AI workloads. The company is also said to be targeting 14 gigawatts of overall computing power next year.

items.title: Micron announces more than $250 billion U.S. investment tied to AI demand
items.summary: Micron said it plans to invest more than $250 billion in the U.S. through 2035, citing surging memory-chip demand from AI. The announcement reinforces the industry trend of massive infrastructure and semiconductor spending to support AI buildouts.

items.title: Meta to build first Canadian data center in Alberta
items.summary: Meta announced plans to build a large data center in central Alberta, its first in Canada, to support AI infrastructure growth. The project reflects the continuing race among tech firms to secure compute capacity for AI development and deployment.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass growth falls short of Microsoft targets
items.summary: IGN reports that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said Game Pass has not grown as Microsoft expected, with the service still tens of millions of subscribers short of earlier goals. The report highlights continued scrutiny of Microsoft’s subscription strategy.

items.title: Sony says PlayStation disc production for new games will end in January 2028
items.summary: VGTimes reports that Sony Interactive Entertainment plans to stop producing physical game discs for new PlayStation 5 releases starting in January 2028, shifting future titles to digital-only distribution. The same development has also drawn strong reaction across gaming media and fans.

items.title: Xbox layoff fallout expands across major studios
items.summary: VGC reports that Microsoft's recent cuts reportedly affected id Software’s coding team and reduced staffing at Obsidian by roughly 60 to 70 developers. The broader restructuring is also said to be pushing Bethesda to refocus around core franchises such as Fallout, The Elder Scrolls, Doom, Quake, and Wolfenstein.

items.title: IO Interactive will keep Project Fantasy independent after the Xbox split
items.summary: VGC reports that IO Interactive has confirmed it will continue Project Fantasy independently after the recent Xbox-related split. The update suggests the game’s development path is changing but remains active.

items.title: State of Decay 3 no longer needs Game Pass release requirement
items.summary: VGC reports that State of Decay 3 is no longer required to launch on Game Pass following Microsoft's broader Xbox changes. The game, first announced in 2020, resurfaced recently and remains in development.

items.title: Nintendo to end Switch sales in Europe in 2027
items.summary: VGC reports that Nintendo of Europe will stop selling the original Nintendo Switch on its store in February 2027. The same report says Nintendo Switch 2 will receive a revision with replaceable batteries in Europe to comply with new EU rules.

items.title: Epic settles lawsuit with Fortnite leaker
items.summary: VGC reports that Epic Games has reached a settlement with former contractor Hayden Cohen, who was accused of leaking confidential information about upcoming Fortnite collaborations. The case had drawn attention because of the scope of the alleged leaks.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 to become a standalone launcher title
items.summary: VGTimes reports that Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 will separate from the unified Call of Duty HQ launcher and operate as its own dedicated title. The change is scheduled for July 7.

items.title: Command & Conquer: Generals — Zero Hour gets native Apple port
items.summary: VGTimes reports that the 2003 RTS Command & Conquer: Generals — Zero Hour now has a native port for macOS, iPhone, and iPad without emulation. The release expands access to a classic strategy game across Apple devices.

items.title: Microsoft reportedly boosts support for MachineGames
items.summary: VGTimes reports that Microsoft is increasing investment in MachineGames following the success of Indiana Jones and the Great Circle and sustained interest in Wolfenstein. The report frames the move as a sign of deeper backing for the studio’s future projects.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Apple raises prices on Mac and iPad models
items.summary: Apple increased prices on some Mac and iPad products, citing higher memory and storage chip costs tied to the broader chip boom. The move highlights how hardware makers are feeling pressure from rising component prices.

items.title: India scraps import duties on some electronics and smartphone parts
items.summary: India removed import duties on selected parts used to make mobile phones and other electronic devices, cutting levies of 7.5% and 5%. The policy change could benefit manufacturers including Apple and Xiaomi.

items.title: SWIFT launches blockchain-based shared ledger for banks
items.summary: Global payments network SWIFT launched a blockchain-based shared ledger with 16 initial banks, including Citi and HSBC. The initiative is aimed at enabling round-the-clock payments and competing with stablecoin-based systems.

items.title: Meta plans in-house production of its own AI smart glasses
items.summary: Meta unveiled a new line of smart glasses designed in-house, signaling a deeper push into wearable devices. The move underscores the company’s effort to control more of its hardware roadmap.

items.title: Microsoft lays off nearly 5,000 workers, including many in Xbox
items.summary: Microsoft announced major layoffs affecting about 3,200 jobs across its Xbox business as part of a broader restructuring. The company is shifting resources toward growth areas while trimming parts of its gaming division.

items.title: Apple and Broadcom expand chip-supply deal
items.summary: Apple said it plans to spend more than $30 billion under a chip-supply agreement with Broadcom. Broadcom will also expand a factory in Colorado as part of the arrangement.

items.title: South Korean chipmakers plan massive manufacturing hub
items.summary: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix plan to invest a combined $518 billion in a new chipmaking hub. The project is designed to meet surging demand tied to the global semiconductor market.

items.title: Meta to manufacture its own AI chip starting in September
items.summary: Meta plans to begin manufacturing an in-house chip from September, according to an internal memo reported by Reuters. The move is intended to boost the company’s computing capacity.
